Transcript:
[00:00] Laura Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining the weekly sync, um we've got Marcus from SE with me. how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Sophie Reyes: good morning, yep all good here. excited to see the numbers.
[00:10] Marcus Patel: hey Sophie, hi Daniel, Priya, quick note — we've got two sets of results to go through: our INT8 runs and the FP8 prototype runs.
[00:18] Daniel Kim: great, let's dive, we mostly care about latency at p95 and any quality regressions for our edge-case prompts.
[00:24] Priya Nair: and from compliance side I'll check audit/logging differences, also KMS impacts if we move to Private.
[00:30] Laura Chen: perfect. quick reminder, the INT8 runs were done on the hosted inference pool (gpu type A100-sim), FP8 was on our experimental kernel on same infra but with slightly different memory layout so you may see small perf variance.
[00:44] Sophie Reyes: can you share the headline numbers first? throughput and latency deltas.
[00:48] Marcus Patel: sure, headline: INT8 gave about 1.9x throughput increase over FP16 baseline, avg token latency dropped ~35% at p50 and p95 improved ~28%. FP8 sits between FP16 and INT8 — roughly 1.4x throughput vs FP16, and latency improvements about 18% p95.
[01:10] Sophie Reyes: ok that's promising. what about quality? we've been flagging hallucination on a subset of prompts.
[01:16] Marcus Patel: right, for quality we ran the 2k labeled eval set you shared. INT8 had a small drop in exact-match and answer F1 — around 2.3% absolute on our metric; FP8 showed about 0.8% delta. hallucination rate rose slightly on INT8 for very long-context prompts ( >2k tokens ), probably due to quantization noise in the KV cache.
[01:36] Sophie Reyes: that matches what we saw in our small local run. any concrete failure examples?
[01:40] Marcus Patel: yes, we've attached a few snippets in the spreadsheet. examples where date arithmetic or precise numeric extraction failed more often under INT8. also a couple of cases where the model repeated tokens, likely due to rounding in attention weights.
[01:54] Daniel Kim: how confident are you in the FP8 stability? you said experimental kernel — is that production-grade?
[01:59] Marcus Patel: good question. FP8 path is still marked experimental; kernels are stable in most workloads but we need a little more validation across sequence lengths. for many RLHF-style completions FP8 maintained fidelity better than INT8. we recommend FP8 for latency-sensitive but quality-aware workloads as a middle ground.
[02:16] Priya Nair: security question: does quantization change any encryption boundaries? like do we serialize different artifact forms to storage that need separate KMS handling?
[02:24] Marcus Patel: no, the model artifacts are stored the same way; quantized weights are still encrypted-at-rest under the same KMS keys. the main difference is around model cache eviction and runtime temp files — we'll document that. Priya, we'll add that to the security notes.
[02:36] Laura Chen: quick pause — Gabe from infra asked if we can get a dedicated throughput run on a Dedicated pool to validate scaling; Daniel, can you take that?
[02:44] Daniel Kim: yes I can coordinate. what's the target config?
[02:47] Marcus Patel: we're thinking 2x A100 equivalent with continuous batching and KV cache size set to your 4k token window. that'll show both throughput and memory pressure.
[02:57] Sophie Reyes: how do batching settings affect quality? we've seen increased batching sometimes increases context mixing.
[03:02] Marcus Patel: batching shouldn't affect model outputs deterministically — it's a scheduling layer — but if you enable aggressive prefix caching or dedup we might see subtle tokenization differences, esp. with quantized kernels. we'll include config notes.
[03:15] Sophie Reyes: any comparison vs running smaller model with more context? like is INT8 on L3 better than FP16 on smaller model?
[03:21] Marcus Patel: depends on use case. in our bench, INT8 on the same model beats smaller models on both latency and quality for most QA tasks, but if your workload is highly numeric/financial then a larger unquantized variant might be safer.
[03:34] Laura Chen: let's talk numbers from the spreadsheet — I uploaded a short summary, link in chat. INT8 p95 token latency: 240ms (baseline FP16 was 335ms). FP8 p95: 275ms. throughput tokens/sec INT8: 980 tps, FP8: 720 tps, FP16 baseline: 520 tps.
[03:52] Sophie Reyes: on our labeled eval set, what was the BLEU/EM drop?
[03:56] Marcus Patel: EM dropped 2.3% for INT8, 0.8% for FP8. BLEU delta small (~1%). recall/precision metrics show most regressions concentrated in long-context numeric extraction.
[04:08] Daniel Kim: any mitigation strategies? aka can we hybrid quantize or fall back to FP16 for certain layers?
[04:12] Marcus Patel: yes — hybrid quantization is an option: keep output/softmax and certain attention projections at FP16 while quantizing key/value and feed-forward per-layer. we tested a layerwise hybrid and saw quality almost recover to FP16 while keeping ~1.5x throughput improvement. there's also per-prompt routing (route to FP16 variant for flagged prompts).
[04:33] Sophie Reyes: per-prompt routing sounds interesting; complexity for us?
[04:36] Laura Chen: it's policy-driven in Redwood: you can define a route rule (e.g., if prompt contains regex or is marked by your app) it hits FP16; otherwise go INT8/FP8. Marcus can send config snippet.
[04:46] Marcus Patel: I'll add a sample policy and the JSON for the routing rules to the repo.
[04:50] Priya Nair: one more sec on audit — are the logs different size with quantized models? we care about retention costs.
[04:55] Marcus Patel: runtime logs are similar; there are additional perf traces for quantization diagnostics if you enable them, but you can toggle that off in production.
[05:03] Sophie Reyes: ok let's capture next steps, I want to validate internal business acceptance criteria. our success metrics: max 1.5% EM drop, p95 under 300ms, and throughput >=700 tps.
[05:15] Laura Chen: good, so on those goals: FP8 meets throughput and p95; EM delta is ~0.8% so within threshold. INT8 gets better throughput but exceeds EM drop threshold on the eval set.
[05:26] Daniel Kim: if we need to stay in EM <1.5% but want more throughput, hybrid per-layer quantization looks promising. can you quantify expected throughput for hybrid?
[05:34] Marcus Patel: hybrid we ran had ~1.5x throughput vs FP16 baseline, p95 ~290ms — so it meets your targets while staying under the EM threshold in our tests.
[05:44] Sophie Reyes: excellent. can we get a more deterministic trial flow? I'd like to run: baseline FP16, INT8, FP8, hybrid on our 1k prompts and see results.
[05:54] Laura Chen: yes that's the plan. Redwood will provide the job configs and the benchmark artifacts. Sophie you'll run the job on your side or want Redwood to run it on a dedicated instance?
[06:02] Sophie Reyes: we'd prefer Redwood runs the dedicated perf job so we get identical infra, then we'll replicate locally for sanity.
[06:09] Marcus Patel: ok we'll schedule that. Daniel and Marcus will spin up the Dedicated pool test.
[06:13] Priya Nair: last question: does using FP8 affect model rollout / versioning semantics? how do we pin to specific quantized artifacts?
[06:21] Marcus Patel: no change to versioning semantics — we keep quantized artifacts as distinct model variants; in Console you'll see model v1.2-fp8 and v1.2-int8. Rollouts and canary work the same way.
[06:30] Sophie Reyes: cool. any notes on fallback policies if we see quality regressions in production?
[06:35] Laura Chen: yes, we can configure automatic fallback to FP16 variant on quality regression or elevated error rates; also can route based on SLO breaches. Marcus we'll add the policy example.
[06:44] Marcus Patel: will do. I'll include sample alert thresholds and the remediation playbook.
[06:49] Laura Chen: ok let's recap next steps — Laura to share full spreadsheet and logs, Marcus to send routing policy and hybrid config, Redwood to run dedicated perf job, Sophie to run internal eval and share results, Priya to confirm security checklist.
[07:02] Sophie Reyes: thanks everyone, that aligns. any other questions?
[07:06] Daniel Kim: none from infra.
[07:08] Priya Nair: all good.
[07:10] Laura Chen: thanks — we'll follow up in email with links.

End of transcript.
